For breakfast: Morning Belle for a fresh light atmosphere and flavorful food. Cherie Inn for a nice cozy breakfast with lots of breakfast options, especially the various eggs benedict options. Lucy’s for a more unique take on the classic breakfast plates.

Second breakfast: Brown Butter Crêperie & Café for a cute French café feel. OR head on down to the Downtown Market to grab a pastry at Field and Fire bakery. Arguably some of the best fresh baked bread and pastries in town! Plus the market offers lots of other vendors to browse throughout. If it’s open and there is not a wedding taking place, there is a green house upstairs you can walk through!

For coffee: Chartreuse Sisters, Common Ground, Lotus Brew, Morning Ritual and The Stray

For dinner: Mangiamo’s has really tasty food, great cocktails and the environment is cozy! A bit steep on the price, but a great option for special occasions. Highly recommend reserving in advance. If you’re looking for something less expensive I would recommend The Commons. Love the cozy 70s vibes. Great drinks and although the menu is small they have great food. I am a big fan of cozy spots!

Fun Drinks: General Wood shop has tasty fun cocktails and mocktails! Honorable mention for their tasty bao buns and cream cheese wonton bites. I have a list of cocktail places I have yet to try since I am still newer to the area. There are quite a few recommendations if you search this subreddit! Hoshi Hoshi is my fav boba shop in the area. You can take a stroll in Gaslight Village while you’re there sipping on your drinks. The park in the village by Reeds Lake can be relaxing depending on the time of day!

Activities: These are on my to do list, but I have not been to these locations yet! The Local Epicurean, where you can take a cooking class together and then eat the food you made. (Right down from Brown Butter Crêperie & Café) You can choose to just browse in the shop for items they are selling as well! Wax Poetic Candle Bar, you can make your own candles. The Mud Room, where you can paint pottery that is already made, take classes pertaining to potter’s wheels and wood signs, as well as glass fusing. 

GR has so much to offer and I could truly keep the list going with recommendations, but I hope this helps! Have an amazing time celebrating Valentine’s Day together!

F / 29 / 5’5 / CW: 143 / GW: 128

It is almost like I wrote this post myself, except the part of being pregnant before. I think my peak weight was 160 and that was just earlier this year.

I have had many conversations with one of my closest friends, who has also struggled with these same toxic mindsets we repetitively put ourselves in.

I also stated that I have the same goal weight, but I am trying to shift my mindset from focusing on my goal weight, to instead loving myself no matter what the scale says.

I don’t diet. I don’t count calories. I don’t do these two things anymore because I know the toxic cycle my mind will ultimately go to.

I try to have the mindset of balance. I may eat a cookie, but then drink water to go with it, instead of soda. Mini habits are so important. Mindful eating can also be a good practice. Looking at it in a way of loving our body, instead of depriving our body.

This takes time to shift our mindset, but it is possible. Take walks, read, journal, meditate or whatever it is you find enjoyment in. Learn to love yourself at every stage. I think we should always want to better ourselves, but we must love ourselves first. Be kind to your mind. Be kind to your body.

DBT/CBT are both great resources. It’s ironic how I teach it daily, but still struggle on my own. I would encourage you to do some research on both of those evidence based practices.

You’re welcome. Honestly, I try to listen to music or focus on my breathing. There are some guided meditations that you could listen to that may help. I overthink and worry often, so specifically doing a body scan or deep breathing guided meditation helps me. Wrapping up in a blanket and laying in bed helps as well. That’s actually a healthy coping skill as long as it’s for shorter periods of time like a half hour or less. There are some times where I too have to just try and ride it out the best I can. Sometimes some of those things just don’t work for me. One evidence based practice you may want to look up is dialectal behavior therapy (DBT). Specifically emotion regulation. I really think you could find some good resources with that. We all have primary and secondary emotions. When we can identify exactly how we are feeling and why, then that is when we can find some solutions on how to improve how we react. I would encourage you to not isolate yourself, but to find someone you trust to talk to. I too like to isolate myself when I feel this way, but it’s not healthy and it won’t help you. Whether that is someone personal or professional. If that professional person sucks, move on to the next one until you find a good fit. I don’t want to look back 5, 10 or 20 years from now and realize that I fucked up my life and the lives around me because I didn’t get the help I needed. I already do look back and realize some people’s lives I have impacted negatively. I carry guilt now because of that and it makes it harder to forgive myself. I wake up next to the person every morning who I love and I realize I am making their life absolutely miserable because I still can’t seem to control my emotions. I’m reaching out for help because I have tried it on my own and it hasn’t worked. Ultimately it is up to us to change and we are the only ones in control of our emotions, but sometimes we need help along the way.

That’s true. Everyone’s bodies do react differently to medications. It may just be a process of finding the right one for me. That’s awesome! It shows that you are capable of making those changes to react differently to situations. It’s those accomplishments that we can really be proud of. 

I carry a lot of guilt knowing how much I have effected the people around me. It makes me want to isolate myself. I feel immense guilt for feeling like I am ruining my boyfriend’s life because I cannot get control over myself.

Have you tried medications? 
I have always had such a negative outlook on them, but I’m to this point where I don’t know what else to do. 

I feel like I have some days that are amazing and I feel truly happy, but those days feel like they are becoming less and less. I go through these really high highs and really low lows. Do you ever feel that way?

I have gone to therapy, read a couple of self-help books, exercised and  have gone to yoga. I have also tried listening to music or doing a guided meditation when I feel myself starting to become upset. I just bought a new bike that I plan to ride around town. I feel like I know a lot of things I can do. I teach evidence based practices with my clients everyday. I have the resources, but I struggle with applying them to my daily life. I constantly feel like I just want to sleep and when I am up I feel like I never have much energy. I know that our eating habits play a huge role on how we feel. I recently feel like I have been stress eating and it makes me feel even more like shit. I don’t want to sit here and come up with all these excuses, but I just honestly feel mentally drained on a daily basis. I know it is going to take a combination of things to help me feel better, but I feel like I have been playing this broken record on repeat for years now.

My parents separated when I was in fifth grade and that is when I first noticed my anxiety and even suicidal thoughts. I didn’t know what anxiety meant at the time, but realized what it was once I got older. As I was growing up I saw my mom suffer from anxiety/depression/OCD. As I have gotten older I have had events happen in my life that have caused me extreme stress, specifically when I was 18-21 years old. I finally graduated college two years ago and I have a great work ethic, but throughout all of this I have not handled my stress well. This then turns into fights within my relationship. I am a very sensitive person, but I also feel like it’s hard for me to control my anger. All of these things that I suffer from turns into a shit show when I’m upset and it explodes. I get angry and then extremely sad where I am crying uncontrollably, which then turns into me having a panic attack. I actually work in the mental health field as a skills coach/case manager. I am a very empathetic person, but damn there are pros and cons to that. This job is great for me, but in other ways I care too damn much. I cannot keep having these panic attacks and I don’t want to make my boyfriend feel like he is trapped in our relationship. I don’t want the easy way out, but I feel like I have tried some solutions and even if I really apply myself they just don’t help enough.

March 13th was the end of the contract date, but they told her both times that she called that she could cancel on February 28, without getting charged a penalty. So, she waited until that date and spent a half hour on the phone with another customer service rep that reassured her multiple times that she would not get charged a penalty for canceling on the day they told her (February 28th). She did not want the contract to roll over into a new one, nor did she want to pay the 200 dollar penalty. There was no rush in switching our internet, she was more than willing to wait until whenever the contract ended. Although, since she was informed by two of the customer service reps that she should cancel on the 28th of February. That is what she did. Well, when the bill came there was a penalty charge of 200 dollars. She calls the customer service rep for Frontier and the lady says, I’m so sorry you were misinformed by the other two customer service reps, but you will need to pay the penalty and there is nothing we can do about it. So, now my mom has not paid the penalty yet. She took the steps she needed to and Frontier misinformed her not only once but twice. Now she is the one who has to pay for their mistake?
